newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Costello comfortable with Australia inflation.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Costello comfortable with Australia inflation.

text.p: Australian Treasurer Peter Costello said in a newspaper interview published on Wednesday that the government was comfortable with the inflation outlook and that Australian official interest rates were set without referring to U.S. interest rate moves.

"We can probably go below the two to three percent underlying inflation target, which makes us very comfortable and we set monetary policy by reference to our own objectives," Costello was quoted as telling the Australian Financial Review.

"The only possible threat that we could see in Australia would be on the wages front and we've made it pretty clear -- I think the Reserve (Bank) has made it pretty clear -- that business has got to factor that into its decision-making," Costello said.
Earlier in the interview Costello said U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan had told him at a meeting that he saw no current threats to inflation.
"He indicated to me that he saw no threats to inflation down the track ... I don't think there is any expectation at the moment that (US) rates are going to rise," Costello said.
Greenspan had said the only possible risk on the inflation front was if wages grew strongly.
"But for an (American) economy which is running at virtually full employment, you don't see a build-up of wage pressure," Costello said.
"So he indicated to me that there is no reason to expect a change on (the) current scene as he sees it," he said.
Australian official cash interest rates were cut by 50 basis points to 7.00 percent on July 31 and economists say another cut is likely before the end of the year.
The board of the Reserve Bank of Australia, which controls monetary policy, met on Tuesday.
